verdict.rationale: Vonage documents parts of how its managed media layer is distributed. It selects the best server in its global network based on a location IP hint, lets you restrict media to regional zones, and supports session migration so clients stay connected when server groups are rotated. It also switches transparently between peer-to-peer and Media Router relaying. It does not explain how capacity scales across nodes or whether autoscaling exists. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of managed autoscaling or capacity scaling across media nodes, architecture detail on multi-region media distribution or cascading, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, the vendor documents how the media layer scales across nodes or regions, whether managed autoscaling or self-hosted clustering

citations.quote: you can set the IP address that the Vonage video platform will use to select the best server to control the session in its global network
To override this optimization and restrict media to a specific region
The `sessionNotification` event is sent when a group of Video API servers for one of your sessions is scheduled to be rotated.
You can prevent clients from being disconnected during server rotation by configuring them to use session migration.
The switch between peer-to-peer relaying and Media Router relaying is handled transparently by the client SDKs.
